title: Sockets on One Machine
summary: Using sockets for local IPC - Winsock start-up, a TCP server bound to 127.0.0.1 and never to every interface, letting the system choose a port and publishing it in a file, Unix domain sockets on Windows, and how sockets compare with named pipes.

cards.q: Why bind a local IPC server to 127.0.0.1 rather than 0.0.0.0?
cards.a: 0.0.0.0 accepts connections from the network and triggers a firewall prompt; 127.0.0.1 accepts only local processes.
The system chooses a free port, avoiding collisions with other programs and other copies of your own.

cards.q: How does a client find a server that bound to port 0?
cards.a: The server writes the chosen port (with its PID and a token) to a file the client knows to read.

cards.q: What controls who may connect to an AF_UNIX socket?
cards.a: The permissions of its path in the file system.
